title: Playwright: multiple browsers, contexts and tracing

videos.script: Since lesson 1, Playwright has been the hands of this course. It clicked, it waited, it read the page. This lesson opens the hands up and looks inside. {{architecture}} Your test runs in Node, outside the browser. Playwright keeps one connection open to it. Commands go down that connection, and events come back up. For Chromium the language on that line is the same one the developer tools speak. {{browsers}} The same tests can run in three engines. You add projects to a configuration, and every test runs once per project. Only Chromium runs on the machine these lessons were recorded on, and the lesson says so where it matters. {{contexts}} A context is a fresh browser profile, with its own cookies and its own storage. Two shoppers can share one browser and see nothing of each other. Then they open the shop's basket, and both see the same one. {{waiting}} Before a click, Playwright waits for the button to be ready. An assertion keeps asking until it is true, or until time runs out. You will see exactly how long that is. {{tracing}} And when a test fails, a trace keeps the evidence. Every action, every request, a picture of every step, in one file. {{end}}
